headline: A 2021 law that extends some COVID-era veterans education rules, adds flexibility for schools and students, and changes several VA home loan and staffing rules.
what_it_does: It extends certain COVID-19 adjustments to VA education benefits through June 1, 2022. It lets the VA waive a second enrollment check for schools that use a flat-rate tuition and fee structure. It exempts some foreign schools and schools using a Department of Education cost template from certain VA and state approving agency requirements, and it allows VA education aid, including a housing stipend, for a last term when a student takes less than half-time credits under specific conditions. It also extends certain VA home loan fee rates through January 14, 2031, and removes the cap on full-time VA staff who provide equal employment opportunity counseling.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans and eligible dependents using VA education benefits
who_it_affects.how: They may receive COVID-era benefit adjustments through June 1, 2022, and may get aid for a final term if they take fewer than half-time credits under the specified conditions.

who_it_affects.group: Schools that accept VA education benefits
who_it_affects.how: Flat-rate tuition schools may be exempt from a second enrollment verification, and some foreign schools and schools using a Department of Education cost template are exempt from certain VA rules.
Certain VA home loan fee rates stay in effect through January 14, 2031.

who_it_affects.group: VA employees who provide equal employment opportunity counseling
who_it_affects.how: The law removes the cap on how many full-time VA employees can do this work.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 21, 2021; the COVID-era education adjustments run through June 1, 2022, and the home loan fee rate extension runs through January 14, 2031.
